proposed_questions.title: Evaluate quality without voting away correctness
proposed_questions.question: A prompt change improves average judge scores but occasionally repeats a booking. How would you evaluate and release it?
answer: Keep the no-duplicate-effect assertion as a deterministic release requirement against authoritative receipts and an independent supplier observation. A higher tone or relevance score cannot compensate for an unauthorized or repeated action. Run language-quality evaluation alongside those invariants, with separate outcomes rather than one blended score.

Freeze representative scenarios, source data, prompt/model/tool versions, judge rubric and judge version. Include ambiguity, refusal, wrong-tool arguments, interruption and no-source cases. Compare baseline and candidate on the same scenarios with repeated runs where justified; inspect uncertainty, severity and subgroup failures. Calibrate a held-out sample against human labels and retain disagreements. The proposed evaluation adds evidence about language behavior; it does not establish returned audio, physical cleanup or production capacity. Current book ROLE-07 states the boundary but does not teach this evaluation design.

followups.question: Can the LLM judge decide whether a supplier mutation happened?
followups.answer: No. Judge language against a rubric; read the business authority and independent supplier records for execution truth. A fluent confirmation sentence may be false, while an ACK loss may hide a committed action.

followups.question: When may a baseline change?
followups.answer: After an intentional reviewed change, with a retained old manifest and an explanation of expected differences. Do not replace it simply to turn a failing run green. Unobserved or skipped required checks remain nonpassing.

proposed_questions.gap: An operational plan for calibrated model-quality evaluation and regression evidence.
proposed_questions.status: Proposed exercise; no model evaluation run.

proposed_questions.title: Canary new sessions while old work remains owned
proposed_questions.question: How would you compare a new agent version without disrupting an ongoing call or repeating background work?
answer: Assign each new conversation to a recorded version/cohort at a trusted dispatch boundary, then keep that assignment stable for its defined lifetime. Record prompt, model, tools and application versions. Run the old and new populations with comparable workload and observe errors, usable first audio and useful task outcomes; explicitly account for timeouts and unresolved business work.

Stop new admission to an old owner before draining its sessions and actual I/O. Session shutdown, an SFU room drain and P1 business-worker recovery have distinct owners. A deployment change must not mint a fresh business identity for an ambiguous earlier command. Define a finite drain deadline and recovery behavior before rollout, plus rollback criteria based on measured harm. Current Cloud documentation describes a bounded old-session completion window; it is not permission to promise arbitrary calls finish forever. The POC has no measured Cloud canary, so this remains a design exercise extending SCALE-06.

followups.question: What does rollback actually undo?
followups.answer: It changes the selected version for eligible future work under the deployment contract. It does not retract spoken audio, reverse supplier effects or erase an accepted command. Reconcile original identities when earlier outcomes are uncertain.

followups.question: Why avoid assigning each turn randomly?
followups.answer: It confounds evaluation with changing prompts, tools or memory within one conversation and can violate compatibility. Choose and record the experimental unit; if turn-level experiments are intentional, define their state and permission semantics explicitly.

proposed_questions.gap: Version/cohort identity, experiment comparability and finite rollout recovery.
proposed_questions.status: Hypothetical deployment experiment; no deployment performed.

proposed_questions.title: Observe the conversation and count the committed outcome
proposed_questions.question: Why can a session have low model latency and high booking counts while users receive no useful result?
answer: Those counters may measure the wrong facts. LLM generation duration excludes parts of the user-perceived path; an agent-local booked flag or tool attempt does not prove a committed supplier change or a delivered completion. Correlate a chosen user input with turn/media observations and the original durable business operation, then count outcomes from retained authoritative receipts.

Keep component, turn, session and business measures separately named. In the pinned Python SDK, metrics_collected contains one typed metric and is deprecated for usage tracking; inspect session usage updates, per-message latency and session-report lifecycle for the selected version. Collect numeric usage in its actual units, preserving missing/unknown values. Use finite aggregate labels and access-controlled sampled traces for identity joins. A replay can add a new observation without adding a new booking. The new exercise would test that distinction rather than repeat the book's general instruction to add observability.

followups.question: Can you estimate cost from a session's wall duration?
followups.answer: Not reliably. Reconcile the actual provider billing quantities: audio seconds or tokens, text tokens, generated characters and other charges under a dated tariff. Include retries and unsuccessful attempts; label estimates and reconcile them with billing.

followups.question: Does a completed report prove the user heard the reply?
followups.answer: No. Pipeline and session observations describe their boundaries. Received/decoded/browser playout evidence is separate, and even playout does not establish human understanding or consent. Preserve that uncertainty in the dashboard and incident narrative.

proposed_questions.gap: A concrete telemetry-contract and duplicate-counting exercise.
proposed_questions.status: Proposed instrumentation exercise; existing diagnostics are not a production monitoring service.

proposed_questions.title: Bound retrieval at the original turn
proposed_questions.question: Where would you retrieve private knowledge for a voice reply, and what if the lookup returns after interruption?
answer: Choose between initial context, an explicit retrieval tool and a turn-completion hook based on whether information is stable, optional or needed before generation. The pinned Python hook receives turn_ctx and new_message; query the accepted message rather than a mutable global transcript. Use bounded asynchronous database/API clients or correctly owned offload, limit retrieved bytes/chunks and carry the original trusted scope and turn identity.

A local timeout or barge-in changes the waiting conversation, not necessarily the lifetime of a running database operation. Retain actual ownership until settlement, and recheck the original generation/lifecycle binding before incorporating the result. Never inject late data into whichever turn happens to be current. Use a truthful no-source or pending response and measure the selected latency boundary; 400 ms is an example budget, not a platform guarantee. Retrieval content remains untrusted evidence and cannot authorize P1 action. The repository's existing fixed-policy records are not a general RAG implementation.

followups.question: Should retrieval run for every utterance?
followups.answer: Only under a deliberate product design. Greetings may need no lookup; structured account facts may belong behind an authenticated tool. Unnecessary retrieval adds cost, exposure and delay. Compare approaches with a representative task and a measured budget.

followups.question: May a retrieved policy instruct the agent to approve a change?
followups.answer: No. Source text cannot grant permissions or replace exact human confirmation. Keep trusted instructions and application authority separate, enforce scope at source access, and test adversarial documents as inert evidence.

proposed_questions.gap: Version-correct retrieval timing and stale asynchronous result handling.
proposed_questions.status: Proposed RAG extension; no vector store or retrieval provider installed/run.

proposed_questions.title: Cache evidence without leaking scope or inventing support
proposed_questions.question: Two users ask the same policy question. When may you reuse the cached retrieval and cite it?
answer: Equivalent wording is only one input. Authorize the second user independently and bind reuse to the permitted tenant/account/document set, document/index version, retrieval configuration and other context that affects the answer. Store original chunk/source/version identifiers and invalidate or revalidate when access or evidence changes. Bound entries and bytes; a TTL is not a complete memory or access policy.

Distinguish an exact normalized-key cache from semantic similarity search. The inspected course's SemanticCache performs the former despite storing an unused embedding/threshold. A real semantic cache needs measured false-hit behavior, especially for negation, numbers and nearly identical policies. On output, carry protected source metadata and speak a concise attribution suited to audio, while retaining inspectable citations in an authorized text view if available. A model naming a document does not prove support. Test unanswerable and conflicting-source queries and keep action permission at the existing exact guard.

followups.question: Does a matching document title establish factual support?
followups.answer: No. Check that the retained version and relevant passage support the claim. The P3 fixed-policy verifier can recompute a small synthetic rule; arbitrary policy prose requires its own retrieval and faithfulness evaluation and an abstention path.

followups.question: Why not clear only the visible answer card?
followups.answer: Presentation state is not the protected identity ledger or source-access contract. Cached retrieval, retained receipts and unresolved processing have different lifetimes. Define their invalidation separately instead of treating a hidden card as deleted authority.

proposed_questions.gap: Access-aware RAG caching and spoken citation verification.
proposed_questions.status: Proposed cache/evidence exercise; no cache benchmark or arbitrary-prose truth guarantee.

proposed_questions.title: Compose graph or MCP logic with one business authority
proposed_questions.question: If you add LangGraph checkpoints or MCP tools, can they replace P1's durable work and exact confirmation?
answer: Not merely by being present. A graph checkpoint preserves the state defined by its checkpointer; MCP standardizes tool exposure and invocation. Neither automatically implements this project's original accepted bytes, exact confirmation, issued execution permission, effect uncertainty and receipt reconciliation. Decide which component owns each fact and keep one recovering owner for the accepted business obligation.

For an experiment, make graph/MCP nodes call narrow public adapters with stable original command identities. Scope graph thread lookup to authenticated conversation bindings and own the checkpointer/client lifecycle. Replaying a node after a crash must reconcile the original operation before any permitted re-invocation. Waiter timeout does not prove a remote effect stopped. Use the selected supported API: current official LiveKit LangChain documentation describes a Python LLMAdapter over a compiled graph; the pinned core exposes MCP server objects through mcp_servers. Do not infer TypeScript plugin parity, transparent function-calling compatibility or general workflow durability from an illustrative wrapper.

followups.question: Can a graph be the sole durable workflow authority instead?
followups.answer: Yes, as a separate explicit architecture with a defined fault model and demonstrated acceptance, consent, idempotency and effect protocol. That is a redesign to evaluate, not permission to let two independent recovery mechanisms own the same operation.

followups.question: Does a discovered typed MCP tool carry mutation consent?
followups.answer: No. Discovery and schema validation describe a callable interface. Bind authenticated scope and exact approved intent at the server-owned boundary, and preserve the external operation's reconciliation identity after uncertain acknowledgment.

proposed_questions.gap: Framework persistence and tool-protocol semantics compared with the concrete P1/P3 authority boundary.
proposed_questions.status: Proposed integration design; no LangGraph/MCP service launched.

proposed_questions.title: Choose providers from a reproducible voice experiment
proposed_questions.question: How would you choose an STT/LLM/TTS stack without trusting a provider ranking table?
answer: Define the actual task, languages/accents, noise, interruption patterns, tool schemas, privacy constraints and acceptable failure behavior. Freeze audio/scenario inputs and model/plugin/prompt versions. Keep other components fixed while changing one, then compare transcription errors, task/tool correctness, first rendered audio, interrupted output and useful completion under the same load and region. Report distributions and failures, not one attractive latency.

Price actual billable units for the selected product and date: STT may charge audio time or tokens, LLMs distinguish input/output/cache/audio units, and TTS may use characters or tokens. Include transport, telephony, hosting, retries and unsuccessful work as relevant. Compare cost per useful resolution alongside quality and privacy. Do not infer that realtime always wins latency, loses tools or costs a fixed multiple. The course tables offer hypotheses; current official capability/pricing and observed evidence must decide. In this checkout, scripted, local_real and provider_real qualifications remain distinct and no silent fallback is authorized.

followups.question: How do you calculate word error rate?
followups.answer: For a specified transcript corpus, WER = (substitutions + deletions + insertions) / reference-word count. Declare normalization and stratify important entities and conditions; one aggregate WER can hide failures on names, numbers or a minority language.

followups.question: Why not sum three average stage timings?
followups.answer: Streaming and endpointing create dependencies and overlap. Define the end-to-end start and finish directly, correlate supporting spans and compare compatible populations. A first provider byte or token is not necessarily first audible output to the caller.

proposed_questions.gap: A concrete quality/capability/cost selection method instead of unstable rankings.
proposed_questions.status: Proposed benchmark plan; no paid provider comparison or current price recommendation.

proposed_questions.title: Restore the right state after a self-hosted failure
proposed_questions.question: If Redis and configuration backups are healthy, what can still be lost when a LiveKit node dies?
answer: Backups and coordination state do not reproduce a running node's WebRTC transports, live media buffers, agent process resources or the application's business receipts. Public self-hosted LiveKit uses Redis for shared room/routing coordination, with a room hosted on a node. Agent servers register over an outbound WebSocket; they are a separate deployment and failure boundary.

Draw an inventory of durable configuration/secrets under protected backup, cluster coordination, live media/session state, agent-local memory and P1 business state. Give each an RPO/RTO and recovery owner. A proposed restore drill should recover configuration with compatible binaries, establish a new usable connection and reconcile accepted business work against original receipts and supplier identities. Graceful room draining is different from forced node loss; forced termination may interrupt calls and leave business recovery pending. Verify configured metrics and network paths instead of assuming default /metrics on 7880. The current local POC has not demonstrated a redundant SFU or regional failover.

followups.question: Does a long Kubernetes termination grace period guarantee no dropped call?
followups.answer: No. It supplies a maximum opportunity to drain under the orchestrator's contract. Active calls may outlast it, dependencies may fail or a node may die abruptly. Define what is admitted, what is retained and how forced-loss recovery is observed.

followups.question: What does a successful health endpoint prove?
followups.answer: Only the endpoint's checks. Demonstrate authenticated connection, actual media in the selected paths and independently verified business progress for those claims. Keep media-server health, worker registration, provider readiness and durable-work recovery separately observable.

proposed_questions.gap: A state-by-state restore exercise spanning media, agents and business authority.
proposed_questions.status: Proposed restore design; no deployment, destructive action or failover performed.

quiz_audit.scope: Read-only review of public quiz props embedded in the already fetched lesson HTML. This is a learning-material audit, not an attempted or completed assessment.
quiz_audit.access_update: This appended overlay supersedes the initial first-question-only SSR visibility limit in the main course review: all publicly embedded prompt, option, marked-selection and explanation props for these 40 lessons have now been read. No interactive quiz state, login, submission, scoring or completion was exercised.
quiz_audit.publication_boundary: No answer-key indices, option letters or copied quiz prompts are included in this report. Chapter and item ordinals identify issues without publishing assessment answers. The eight proposed book questions predate this overlay and were not rewritten from quiz prompts.
method: Read all 134 prompts, all provided options, the embedded marked selection and every explanation from retained .quiz.json files.
Distinguished invalid distractors, which are expected in a multiple-choice quiz, from errors or unjustified guarantees in a marked answer or its explanation.
Cross-checked material API and behavior claims against official references and installed livekit-agents 1.8.11 source. No snippet was executed and no provider, deployment or assessment was invoked.

Used chapter/item ordinals only for traceability. A structurally valid key is not a guarantee of technical correctness. Architecture ambiguity is reported separately from a demonstrably false runtime/API claim.

structural_integrity.limit: This is static data validation, not quiz execution or an endorsement of all marked answers.

findings.issue: The quiz reinforces the unsupported AgentTest harness and equates removing media transport with a network-free, fully repeatable behavioral test.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Separate deterministic mocked unit tests from model-dependent behavioral judgments. Teach the pinned AgentSession.run / RunResult and mock_tools interfaces; declare the model/judge, network use, seeds if supported, and repeatability limits.

verification.claim: AgentSession.run takes a user_input string and returns RunResult.

findings.issue: Several explanations present judge consistency, a fixed regression-score delta and a sampling percentage as if they establish reliability or statistical significance. A low tone score is assigned a single prompt-related cause.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Use anchored rubrics as a starting point, then calibrate against labeled cases and repeated judgments. Choose a threshold and sample size from observed variance, cohort size and acceptable error; inspect recordings, prompts and judge disagreement before diagnosing tone.

findings.issue: The example assigns variants using a session identifier, but the marked explanation claims that a returning caller necessarily receives the same variant. A new session identifier can place that caller in another variant.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Choose the assignment unit explicitly: session-level consistency uses a session ID; caller-level consistency needs an authorized stable identity or persisted assignment. Keep tenant scope and privacy requirements explicit.

verification.course_evidence: The production-evaluation lesson code hashes session_id; this is not a stable caller identity contract.

findings.issue: The explanations describe rolling or blue-green release as allowing every current caller to finish, without stating the drain budget.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Explain admission cutover separately from finite draining and forced termination. LiveKit managed rolling deployments give old instances up to one hour for active sessions; a custom platform needs its own verified grace and recovery policy.

verification.claim: Managed old instances have a finite one-hour session-completion window.

findings.issue: The autoscaling explanation treats an I/O-waiting session as occupying an entire worker that cannot accept another session. The certification explanation calls workers stateless and denies managed automatic scaling.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Distinguish agent server capacity, isolated session/job processes and application durability. Scale using measured session counts plus CPU, memory, event-loop and provider limits; an idle CPU alone is insufficient. Managed Cloud deployment and custom worker orchestration are different operating modes.

findings.issue: The explanation claims identical text and voice always produce identical TTS audio and presents a fixed savings range without workload evidence.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Caching an approved audio artifact can avoid another synthesis call even when the provider is nondeterministic. Key by all relevant rendering settings and model/version, enforce scope and retention, and measure hit rate, quality and net savings.

verification.claim: Provider documentation explicitly declines a determinism guarantee, including when a seed is supplied.

findings.issue: The question assumes a wide UDP range is always required; the explanation suggests separate allocation for each media track.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Firewall rules follow the configured ICE transport. LiveKit supports a single UDP mux port instead of the range. Distinguish participant transport allocation from track count and include TCP/TURN fallbacks where configured.

verification.claim: Setting rtc.udp_port enables UDP mux and replaces use of the configured port range.

findings.issue: The upgrade explanation promises a short reconnect after forced node loss. The backup explanation can be read as saying media cannot be stored at all.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Differentiate draining live rooms, abrupt media-node loss, SDK reconnect behavior and recovery of the application workflow. A healthy replacement does not prove restoration of the old session. Recordings can be retained, but a recording is not a backup that resumes the original live WebRTC transport.

findings.issue: The explanation says a custom turn hook must call a parent implementation or the augmented context will never reach generation. In the pinned Python SDK, that default hook is a no-op.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Use the actual two-argument on_user_turn_completed hook, mutate its supplied ChatContext through supported methods, and follow the session pipeline. A parent call may be appropriate for a custom subclass, but is not the SDK generation switch described here.

verification.claim: The default on_user_turn_completed signature takes turn_ctx and new_message; its body is pass.

findings.issue: The explanations turn an example division of labor into an exclusive rule: RAG for unstructured data, MCP for structured data, and LiveKit RAG only through a model-invoked search tool.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Separate retrieval technique from tool transport. MCP can expose retrieval, and RAG can use initial context, a turn hook or a tool. Select based on freshness, latency, access checks and when the information is needed; names and descriptions influence tool selection alongside other context and policy.

verification.claim: The official guide describes initial-context, tool and turn-hook integration options.

findings.issue: The LangGraph item calls asyncio.wait_for a hard response-time guarantee. The CRM scenario similarly treats a timer as sufficient to guarantee a bounded response.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: A timeout initiates cooperative cancellation; wait_for can exceed its timeout while cancellation completes. Keep the actual task/client lifetime owned, set underlying I/O deadlines where supported, preserve late effect truth, and prevent stale background enrichment from entering a newer turn.

verification.claim: Python documents that wait_for waits for cancellation and total wait time may exceed the timeout.

findings.issue: A falling retrieval hit rate is diagnosed as a knowledge-coverage gap without considering other changes.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Check query mix, tenant authorization filters, embedding/index versions, retrieval thresholds, cache changes and source freshness before concluding that documents are missing. Hit rate does not establish grounded answer correctness.

findings.issue: Provider latency/cost ratios, wrapper transparency and pipeline overlap are stated too broadly. The pipeline descriptions also conflict about whether LLM work can overlap the user/STT turn. One integration explanation reduces all chains to linear execution.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Use the pinned adapter API and verify required model features. Describe preemptive generation, final turn commitment and TTS overlap separately. Benchmark the actual provider/model/region, language, audio corpus and tool workload; include cached-token pricing and billed units. Treat architecture families as patterns, not universal capability or timing claims.

findings.issue: The room-lifecycle explanation states that rooms disappear as soon as the last participant leaves, omitting configurable departure retention and explicit creation.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Rooms can be created explicitly or on demand. Explain empty_timeout and departure_timeout separately; use the actual configuration when reasoning about reconnect and dispatch-on-creation.

verification.claim: CreateRoom supports empty_timeout and departure_timeout with distinct meanings.

findings.issue: The explanation says interrupted speech never resumes. The pinned SDK can pause and resume a false interruption when configured and supported by the audio output.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Separate a genuine committed new user turn from noise/backchannel classified as false interruption. Trace the configured interruption policy, paused output capability and whether a newer response superseded the old one.

verification.claim: A configured false interruption can restore paused speech and call audio_output.resume when the guarded conditions hold.

findings.issue: The certification item labels connection and error screens as SDK agent activity states. That enum differs from the pinned SDK.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Keep room/session connection state, agent activity state and application failure state separate in the frontend. Map them explicitly instead of assuming a single lifecycle or deriving business outcome from an animation.

verification.claim: Pinned AgentState contains initializing, idle, listening, thinking and speaking.

findings.issue: The tool explanation conflates the Python decorator with the TypeScript API and describes strings as the only tool result shape.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Teach Python function_tool and Node llm.tool as separate language APIs. Results may be structured values converted for the model; speech-ready strings are a design preference, not a universal runtime restriction. Type/schema validation does not grant mutation authority.

verification.claim: The official definition guide shows Python and Node APIs and structured return values.

findings.issue: The token explanation says agent dispatch cannot be configured in a token, which contradicts the supported room configuration mechanism. It also treats data publishing as mandatory for every voice user.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Protect server signing credentials and issue only the media/data grants a client actually needs. RoomConfiguration.agents can request dispatch when a token creates a new room; it does not redispatch into an existing room. Data permission depends on the chosen text/data features.

verification.claim: Official dispatch docs support RoomAgentDispatch entries in a participant access token, applied on room creation.

findings.issue: The RPC option implies JSON schemas and typed responses are supplied by the transport. The distinction from model tools is otherwise useful.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: RPC carries application payload strings and returns a string or transport/application error. Define and validate your own request/response schema, authenticate the calling participant, and use the same business authority as other entry points; an RPC response still is not a durable effect receipt.

verification.claim: The API accepts a payload string and returns a string; JSON is an application-selected format.

findings.issue: The telephony explanation calls the caller a STANDARD participant. The channel scenario says only the frontend differs and the agent need not consider the channel.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: A SIP caller is a room participant with SIP kind and SIP-specific attributes. Reuse core workflow/tools while handling DTMF, caller-identity trust, transfer semantics and channel presentation through explicit supported adapters and policy.

verification.claim: Official participant documentation identifies telephony callers with Participant.Kind SIP.

findings.issue: Several architecture scenarios have multiple defensible designs, yet their explanations present one as universally superior without enough requirements. Specialization is also described as ensuring agents never cross domains.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Treat these as design discussions: ask about workflow boundaries, access control, language coverage, operational cost and failure recovery. Single-agent tools, specialized agents, channel-aware variants, shadowing and language-specific configurations can each be appropriate. Prompt separation or a generated handoff summary does not enforce authority or prove facts.

findings.issue: The item equates a non-streaming TTS provider with waiting for the entire LLM response. It overlooks adapting an incoming text stream into sentence-sized synthesis calls.
findings.recommended_learning_correction: Distinguish LLM text streaming, a provider speech stream and the SDK stream adapter. A non-streaming provider can still synthesize completed chunks before the full model response, with different latency/prosody tradeoffs; interruption behavior is a separate output concern.

verification.claim: The adapter synthesizes each incoming tokenized segment through the wrapped TTS and forwards frames.

additional_primary_sources.verified_claim: Timeout cancellation may take longer than the requested wait; cancellation does not establish that external effects did not happen.
The seed parameter makes deterministic sampling a best effort; exact output determinism is not guaranteed.
Optional rtc.udp_port enables single-port UDP mux in place of the UDP range.
Room creation exposes separate empty and departure timeouts.
Python uses function_tool; Node uses llm.tool. Structured return values are supported and converted for model consumption.
Participant tokens can configure agent dispatch entries. This is applied when the token creates the room, not when it joins an existing room.
RPC payload and response are strings; applications select formats such as JSON and own validation.
A telephony caller is a SIP-kind participant with SIP-specific attributes.

learning_recommendation.overall: Use the public quizzes as prompts for explaining and tracing behavior, with the corrected source register beside them. Do not memorize the marked responses as API authority or use a completion badge as production-readiness evidence.
highest_priority_corrections: Separate session-cohort assignment from caller-cohort identity.
Treat timeout and drain budgets as finite operational boundaries, not proof that work stopped.
Replace the hook, agent-state and token-dispatch claims with pinned APIs.
Distinguish job state, application durability and the Cloud/custom deployment modes.
Use measured provider/rendering behavior instead of deterministic-TTS or fixed savings/latency claims.
learning_recommendation.certification_course: All 40 public items in 7.1 were inspected. The practical scenarios are useful oral-design exercises, but several have requirement-dependent alternatives and several API/lifecycle explanations need correction. Official affiliation, accreditation or employer recognition of this certification was not established by this audit.

suggested_reading_route.task: Read the existing project authority and failure-boundary questions, then explain one failure schedule without the quiz.
Study the proposed model-evaluation, turn-bound retrieval and benchmark additions with pinned official examples.
Compare deployment/drain, integration ownership and state-restore cases; state which outcomes remain unknown.

learning_recommendation.book_action: Keep the current audited book unchanged until the user selects additions. The eight original proposals remain the recommended addition set; the quiz overlay strengthens their caveats rather than creating copied assessment questions.

limits: No video was watched and no live quiz or exam was attempted.
Static source review cannot qualify timing, cost savings, model quality, capacity, deployment safety or provider compatibility.
Only the installed Python Agents version was pinned; an optional LangChain integration installation and cross-language parity were not established.
No official certification status was inferred from the course name, footer, quiz data or claimed curriculum coverage.
